T-L's new touch panel boosts management of linear sprinklers

The PLT panel will make its U.S. debut in 2027, bringing precision to linear irrigation systems.

Curt Arens,senior editor of Nebraska Farmer,Nebraska FarmerOctober 22, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

At Husker Harvest Days in Grand Island, Neb., this past September, T-L Irrigation engineering manager Neal Schlautman discussed the development of the new touch control panel for the company’s innovative linear irrigation systems. The new panels, which offer sub-inch accuracy and control for linear systems, will be released in the U.S. early in 2027. Curt Arens 

link

Center pivots are by far the most utilized irrigation systems in Nebraska and across the Plains states. But linear systems are gaining interest.

“In well-developed irrigation areas like Nebraska, we are seeing an increase in linear interest because the nice square fields have all been developed with pivot irrigation because that makes the most [return on investment],” said John Thom, vice president of T-L Irrigation Co., which is based in Hastings, Neb. “Now the other ground that is longer and rectangular in shape or odd-shaped that has been flood-irrigated is being converted over, and linears seem to fit better on those fields, compared to pivots.”

Thom said that in some parts of the U.S., where land is extremely expensive, farmers want every inch of every field developed for irrigation. “In those cases,” he noted, “linears have been a good solution.”

LeRoy Thom founded T-L in 1955, and the company sold more than 300 miles of Tractor Tow Line sprinkler irrigation systems the following year. They built their first self-propelled circular system in 1969, featuring a unique continuous move hydrostatic drive system.

Related:Claas invests $10M in Nebraska research center

T-L Vice President John Thom said at HHD that center pivots have always been popular, but linear irrigation systems are gaining in use, particularly in parts of the U.S. where land is so expensive that growers want to efficiently irrigate every inch they can. In addition, overseas, vast fields offer linears the ability to irrigate efficiently without disruption from county line roads or other obstacles.

New panel for linears

While T-L has been producing center pivots and linear sprinkler systems that are sold around the world, the company is now preparing to introduce a new precision touch panel to U.S. growers in early 2027, specifically for their linear systems. This development has been in the research and testing phase for about a year and a half.

“Our center pivot Precision Point Touch panel has been well-received with growers,” said Neal Schlautman, T-L engineering manager. “So, we have adapted that panel to our linear system, and we’re calling it our Precision Linear Touch panel or PLT.”

With infield introduction this winter tentatively scheduled in Australia and New Zealand, the new PLT panels are equipped with a 7-inch color graphic touch screen that makes it easy to see what is going on.

“With linears, it is harder to visualize what is going on in the field, so the full color graphic touch screen makes it much simpler to monitor and control the linear system operation,” Schlautman said. “These new panels incorporate water application and direction control, in addition to water pump control, end gun control, auxiliary relay control, and auto stop or auto reverse locations. The new PLT panels will work with hose drag and ditch feed linear systems.”

The T-L linear system itself incorporates RTK GPS navigation for sub-inch accuracy, with a package that includes the base station eliminating the need for a subscription. There are GPS antennas on every linear, and the system tracks multiple constellations, reducing signal loss caused by tree lines and other obstacles. Plus, there is no electronic interference from power lines.

Related:Latest grain equipment proves to be smarter, faster and safer

The PLT panel and the RTK GPS Rover work together to bring real-time information to the grower through the PLT panel, so they can see it visually and note any cross-track error to the tenth of an inch that the linear may be off the path, Schlautman said.

Full control

“The PLT panel controls both the left- and right-end towers for direction and speed control to keep the system on path,” he said. “If we get more than a half-inch off the path, it starts to steer while still keeping the continuous movement of the entire system.”

Thom added that T-L has one of the best linear systems on the market with simple but accurate GPS navigation system incorporated with the PLT panel for continuous movement and uniformity of water application.

Because T-L linear systems use up to 60% less water than flood irrigation and can cover almost 98% of a rectangular field, their popularity is growing in areas where they make sense. When their new touch control panel, designed specifically for linear systems, is released in 2027, it will make it easier for growers to track and control their linear systems.

Related:Lindsay invests $90M to modernize Nebraska facility

About the Author

Curt Arens

senior editor of Nebraska Farmer, Nebraska Farmer

Curt Arens began writing about Nebraska’s farm families when he was in high school. Before joining Farm Progress first as a field editor in 2010, and then as editor of Nebraska Farmer in 2021, he had worked as a freelance farm writer for 27 years for newspapers and farm magazines, including Nebraska Farmer. His real full-time career during this period was farming his family’s fourth-generation land near Crofton, Neb., where his family raised corn, soybeans, wheat, oats, alfalfa, cattle, hogs and Christmas trees.

Curt and his wife, Donna, have four children: Lauren, Taylor, Zachary and Benjamin. They are active in their church and St. Rose School in Crofton, where Donna teaches. The family now rents out their crop ground to a neighbor, but still lives on the same farm first operated by Curt's great-grandparents. The family runs a few cows and other assorted 4-H and FFA critters.

Previously, the 1986 University of Nebraska animal science graduate wrote a weekly rural life column, developed a farm radio program and wrote books about farm life. He received media honors from the Nebraska Forest Service, Center for Rural Affairs, Nebraska Association of County Extension Boards and Nebraska Association of Natural Resources Districts.

He wrote about the spiritual side of farming in his 2008 book, Down to Earth: Celebrating a Blessed Life on the Land, garnering a Catholic Press Association award.

translationZh:
在内布拉斯加州格兰德岛今年9月举办的Husker Harvest Days展会上，T-L Irrigation工程经理Neal Schlautman介绍了公司为创新型线性灌溉系统开发的新型触摸控制面板。这款新面板可为线性系统提供亚英寸级精度和控制，将于2027年初在美国发布。

中心支轴式喷灌机是内布拉斯加州及整个平原州迄今为止使用最广泛的灌溉系统。但线性系统的关注度正在上升。

“在内布拉斯加州这样的发达灌溉区，我们看到线性系统的兴趣在增加，因为漂亮的方形地块都已开发为支轴式灌溉，因为那能带来最高的投资回报率，”总部位于内布拉斯加州黑斯廷斯的T-L Irrigation公司副总裁John Thom说。“现在那些较长、矩形或形状不规则、此前采用漫灌的土地正在转换，与支轴式相比，线性系统似乎更适合这些地块。”

Thom表示，在美国一些土地极其昂贵的地区，农民希望每一寸土地都得到灌溉开发。“在那些情况下，”他指出，“线性系统是一个很好的解决方案。”

LeRoy Thom于1955年创立了T-L公司，次年公司售出了超过300英里的拖曳式喷灌灌溉系统。他们于1969年建造了第一台自走式圆形系统，采用独特的连续移动静液压驱动系统。

T-L副总裁John Thom在HHD展会上表示，中心支轴式一直很受欢迎，但线性灌溉系统的使用正在增加，尤其是在美国土地昂贵到种植者希望高效灌溉每一寸土地的地区。此外，在海外，广阔田地让线性系统能够高效灌溉，而不受县界道路或其他障碍物的干扰。

**线性系统新面板**

T-L一直在生产销往全球的中心支轴式和线性喷灌系统，公司现在准备于2027年初向美国种植者推出一款新的精密触摸面板，专门用于其线性系统。这一开发已处于研究和测试阶段约一年半。

“我们的中心支轴Precision Point Touch面板受到了种植者的好评，”T-L工程经理Neal Schlautman说。“因此，我们将该面板适配到我们的线性系统上，称之为Precision Linear Touch面板，简称PLT。”

新的PLT面板暂定于今年冬季在澳大利亚和新西兰进行田间首发，配备7英寸彩色图形触摸屏，便于查看运行情况。

“对于线性系统，很难直观地看到田间正在发生什么，因此全彩图形触摸屏使监控和控制线性系统运行变得简单得多，”Schlautman说。“这些新面板集成了施水与方向控制，以及水泵控制、末端喷枪控制、辅助继电器控制和自动停止或自动反转位置。新的PLT面板将与拖管式和沟渠供水线性系统配合使用。”

T-L线性系统本身采用RTK GPS导航，精度达亚英寸级，配套包含基站，无需订阅服务。每台线性设备上都装有GPS天线，系统可跟踪多个星座，减少因树线和其他障碍物造成的信号丢失。此外，不受电力线的电子干扰。

Schlautman说，PLT面板和RTK GPS漫游器协同工作，通过PLT面板向种植者提供实时信息，使他们能够直观地看到并注意到线性设备可能偏离路径的横向误差，精确到十分之一英寸。

**全面控制**

“PLT面板控制左右端塔的方向和速度，以保持系统在路径上，”他说。“如果我们偏离路径超过半英寸，它就开始转向，同时保持整个系统的连续移动。”

Thom补充说，T-L拥有市场上最好的线性系统之一，其简单而准确的GPS导航系统与PLT面板相结合，实现连续移动和施水均匀性。

由于T-L线性系统比漫灌节水高达60%，且可覆盖矩形田地近98%的面积，其在适用地区的受欢迎程度正在增长。当专为线性系统设计的新触摸控制面板于2027年发布时，将使种植者更容易跟踪和控制其线性系统。
